scenes.say: Ever wonder how Kafka remembers exactly which messages you've read, even after a crash? Let's talk about offsets.

scenes.label: Offset
scenes.sub: Tracks a consumer’s position in a partition.
scenes.say: An offset is just a number that marks your spot in a partition. It's how Kafka keeps track of what each consumer has read.
You can let Kafka commit offsets automatically, or do it manually after processing. Manual commits give you more control and reliability.
In Java, you call commit sync after handling a batch. This makes sure you only move the offset forward when processing succeeds.

scenes.question: Is auto-commit always reliable?
scenes.wrong: Yes, it's safe for all cases.
scenes.right: No, manual commit is safer for at-least-once.
scenes.say: Don't fall for this: auto-commit might skip messages if you crash mid-processing. Manual commit is safer when you need reliability.
